newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies mixed, trade choppy on US labor data.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies mixed, trade choppy on US labor data.

text.p: IMM currency futures were mixed, chopping around in-line with the U.S. debt markets following the U.S. employment numbers, forex traders and analysts said.
"There is no clear signal how to play these numbers," Dave Durrant, senior currency analyst at IDEA, Inc, said.

U.S. April nonfarm payrolls rose 142,000, compared to average trade estimates for a rise of 211,000. March payrolls were downwardly revised to a rise of 139,000 from the original report of up 175,000.
However, the jobless rate fell to 4.9 percent, versus forecasts the rate would stay steady from March's 5.2 percent.

June Swiss francs and Canadian dollars widened opening gains, while June marks and yen briefly reversed losses, as the U.S. bonds rallied and the U.S. long bond yield fell in a knee-jerk reaction to the payrolls number.

The U.S. average workweek declined to 34.6 hours from March's 34.9 hours, and average hourly earnings fell to $12.14 from $12.15 in March. Traders, on average, were looking for average hourly earnings to rise 0.3 percent from March.
"Those were soft numbers, but U.S. bonds turned around on the unemployment rate," Durrant said.
U.S. June T-bonds, which had been steadily rising ahead of the numbers, jumped to 110-10/32, but just as quickly slipped back towards the 109-23/32 level.
The choppiness in the U.S. debt markets where Eurodollars futures traded in fast-market conditions was reflected in the currency pits.
The dollar, which weakened on the prospect for lower U.S. rates, managed to recover and pushed June marks and yen back into negative territory.
June Swiss francs found light support from comments by Bruno Gehrig, a Swiss National Bank board member.
Prior to the opening of pit trade, Gehrig said Switzerland could not remedy basic structural problems facing the economy by relaxing monetary policy excessively.
However, Durrant said the dollar would find bids in the near- to intermediate-term. He pegged support at 1.72 dollar/mark and 126.00 dollar/yen.
"We still have good growth in the U.S., and in general the U.S. asset markets are rallying," Durrant said. "There is no reason for U.S. investors to look elsewhere."
The 1.72 spot level corresponds to $0.5831 in June marks, and 126.00 spot currently equals about $0.007984 in June yen.
Meanwhile, Canadian dollar futures continued to rally, while sterling remained sharply lower from GLOBEX levels. September sterling fell through the GLOBEX low of $1.6000.
Durrant said profit-taking in the wake of the Labor Party's victory should dry up in the medium-term.
"They have a strong economy and I expect them to raise rates next week," he said about next week's U.K. meeting.

At 0815 CDT/1315 GMT, June yen was off $0.000011 at $0.007935, marks were down $0.0015 at $0.5809, Swiss francs fell $0.0005 at $0.6830, sterling lost $0.0130 at $1.6096 and Canadian dollars were up $0.0022 at $0.7255.
